The supplied configuration sets discard_no_hit: true. Omitting the key entirely resolves to false, so deleting it changes the behaviour.

docs.title: How auto picks the genus
docs.text:
auto_vote determines how the dominant genus is selected from the BlobTools assignments.

auto_vote Measure Genus selected bp (default) Sum of contig lengths assigned to each genus Greatest total sequence length contigs Number of contigs assigned to each genus Greatest contig count

For example:

Contig Assigned genus Length contig_1 GenusA 5,000,000 bp contig_2 GenusB 60,000 bp contig_3 GenusB 45,000 bp contig_4 GenusB 8,000 bp

bp selects GenusA, with 5,000,000 bp compared with 113,000 bp for GenusB. contigs selects GenusB, with three contigs compared with one, and can therefore remove the chromosome. This is the reason for the length-based default. Either setting can remove genuine plasmids assigned to a different genus; see plasmid retention.

An exact tie is resolved alphabetically by genus name. The calculation is made before applying genus aliases. With discard_no_hit: true, no-hit does not participate in the calculation.

The log records the measure and selected genus, for example Auto vote by bp: kept genus GenusA. The composition report records both measures so that their agreement can be inspected.

The same measure is applied to the retained, genus-assigned contigs to choose the genus written to {sample}_kept_genus.txt. This is passed to Bakta as a genus hint; see Annotation. The log records it as Genus given to Bakta: GenusA.

docs.title: Genus aliases
docs.text:
The selector uses a genus-alias table in auto and include modes to reduce removal of contigs assigned to certain closely related genera. Aliases do not apply to exclude: only the genera explicitly listed are excluded.

This table is a filtering safeguard. It does not reconcile the taxonomies of NCBI, GTDB and LPSN, and should not be treated as a taxonomic classification.

docs.title: Settings for a batch or an individual sample
docs.text:
Key Scope Behaviour mode All samples, unless overridden Primary filtering policy auto_vote All samples Dominant-genus measure; also used for the Bakta genus hint discard_no_hit All samples, unless overridden Handling of contigs without a taxonomic assignment long_read_mode All hybrid samples Decision policy for the second screen; does not modify the final assembly include_genera All samples, unless overridden Base list of genera to retain in include mode exclude_genera All samples, unless overridden Base list of genera to remove in exclude mode exclude_genera_file All samples, unless overridden File whose entries are added to exclude_genera; an override row's exclude_genera replaces both include_genera_by_sample Samples named in the file Entries are added to that sample's include list sample_overrides Samples named in the file Non-empty fields replace the corresponding settings for that sample

include_genera and exclude_genera accept inline lists such as [Bacillus, Priestia] or strings separated by semicolons, commas or tabs. Whitespace around separators is removed. The other three genus-list/override keys are file paths, not inline mappings.

Settings are resolved in this order:

  1. Read the batch settings.
  2. Add entries from include_genera_by_sample for the current sample.
  3. Apply non-empty fields from its sample_overrides row.

docs.title: Configuration examples
docs.text:
The following examples show changes to make in a copy of the supplied configuration. They are not complete configuration files.

Retain known target genera throughout the batch. For one genus, supply a single name; for several, separate the names as shown.

parameters:
  decontamination:
    mode: include
    include_genera: "Bacillus;Priestia;Peribacillus"

Remove known contaminants. An optional file extends the inline list.

parameters:
  decontamination:
    mode: exclude
    exclude_genera: "Cutibacterium;Ralstonia"
    exclude_genera_file: /path/to/known_contaminants.txt

The file contains one genus per line. Blank lines and comments beginning with # are ignored.

# Additional contaminant genera
GenusB
GenusC

Add genera for selected samples. The file is tab-separated with columns sample and genus. A sample may appear on multiple rows or have several genera in one cell.

parameters:
  decontamination:
    mode: include
    include_genera: "Bacillus"
    include_genera_by_sample: /path/to/extra_genera.tsv

sample	genus
isolate1	Lysinibacillus
isolate2	Lysinibacillus;Brevibacillus

isolate1 retains Bacillus and Lysinibacillus; isolate2 retains Bacillus, Lysinibacillus and Brevibacillus. Other samples retain Bacillus and its aliases, such as Priestia, Peribacillus and Paenibacillus.

Override a sample's policy or lists. In sample_overrides, sample and mode are required columns. include_genera, exclude_genera and discard_no_hit are optional. Non-empty cells replace the existing setting; empty cells leave it unchanged.

parameters:
  decontamination:
    mode: auto
    sample_overrides: /path/to/overrides.tsv

sample	mode	include_genera	exclude_genera	discard_no_hit
isolate3	off			
isolate4	include	Bacillus;Lysinibacillus		
isolate5	exclude		Cutibacterium	false

isolate3 retains all contigs. isolate4 uses an include list containing Bacillus and Lysinibacillus, replacing any previous include list. isolate5 removes only contigs assigned to Cutibacterium and retains unclassified contigs. Preserve the tab delimiters, including those around empty cells, when creating this file.

Adding to a list and replacing it have different effects

If the batch includes Bacillus, adding Lysinibacillus through include_genera_by_sample retains both genera for that sample. Setting include_genera to Lysinibacillus in sample_overrides replaces the list, so only Lysinibacillus and its applicable aliases are included.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
The primary screen is defined in workflow/rules/shared/10_decontam.smk. It combines taxonomic evidence and coverage, then applies the selection policy.

---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    D["Draft assembly"] --> T["BLAST taxonomic evidence"]
    D --> M["Mapping coverage"]
    T --> B["BlobTools contig table"]
    M --> B
    B --> S["Taxonomy-based selection"]
    S --> F["Retained assembly"]
    S --> A["Decision and composition files"]

docs.title: Taxonomic assignment
docs.text:
BLAST+ searches the draft contigs against the NCBI nucleotide database with megablast. The output contains the matching taxonomy IDs, alignment statistics and subject titles. parameters.nt_version selects the database subdirectory, core_nt or nt_prok.

parameters:
  nt_version: core_nt

The reference database and NCBI taxonomy files must be prepared as described in Reference databases. BlobTools uses nodes.dmp and names.dmp to resolve taxonomic assignments. Missing taxonomy files stop the workflow before the corresponding jobs run.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
Mapping the sample's reads to the draft assembly provides per-contig read depth. Differences in depth can help with inspection of possible contaminants, although the selector does not use this information.

Workflow mode Mapping method illumina, hybrid Bowtie2 mapping of the paired-end Illumina reads nanopore minimap2 with the map-ont preset contigs minimap2 alignment of the contigs against themselves

The mapping output is contaminants/{sample}_map.bam and its .bai index. These are temporary files, retained until their dependent jobs finish. Where reads are available, the mapping also supports Qualimap.

Self-alignment does not measure sequencing depth

In contigs mode, reads are unavailable. BacFlux aligns the assembly against itself to generate the BAM file required by BlobTools. This alignment does not provide independent read-depth evidence, so its coverage values should not be interpreted as sequencing depth. This mode has no Qualimap report.

docs.title: Combining the evidence
docs.text:
BlobTools combines contig length, GC content, coverage and taxonomic evidence. Its bestsum rule sums BLAST bit scores by taxon to assign contigs at each reported taxonomic rank. The selector uses the genus assignment from contaminants/bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt.

This table is retained so that the evidence supporting the decisions can be examined. Neither the coverage values nor the GC content determine which contigs the selector retains.

docs.title: Applying the policy
docs.text:
select_contigs runs workflow/scripts/10_decontam/select_contigs_by_taxonomy.py. The script reads the genus assignments, resolves the settings for each sample, applies the policy and records the result for each contig in contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv.

If no contigs are retained, the primary selection step fails. It writes the decisions file before failing, so the reasons can be inspected instead of passing an empty assembly to downstream analyses.

docs.title: BLAST of the final long-read assembly
docs.text:
In nanopore and hybrid modes, blast_final_contigs repeats the BLAST search on contigs_final.fasta and writes {sample}_final_blastout. This provides BLAST evidence with the contig identifiers used in the final assembly for the plasmid stage's supplementary check.

In hybrid mode, the primary search used the Illumina draft, whose contig identifiers differ from those in the Nanopore assembly. In nanopore mode, polishing occurs after the primary search and may affect the headers. The second search avoids relying on identifiers from the earlier assembly. It also supplies the taxonomy for the hybrid final-assembly screen. In illumina and contigs modes, the plasmid stage reuses the primary BLAST table.

docs.title: The second screen in hybrid
docs.text:
The final hybrid assembly is built from Nanopore reads, whereas the primary selection step filters the Illumina draft. With parameters.hybrid.short_read_guidance: false (the default), long-read filtering uses length and quality without the decontaminated Illumina reads as a reference. The primary taxonomic filter therefore does not remove contaminant long reads before assembly.

A separate screen combines long-read coverage of contigs_final.fasta with the final-assembly BLAST results. It uses the same selector, genus lists, aliases, auto_vote and discard_no_hit, with its policy set by parameters.decontamination.long_read_mode.

This screen reports decisions without modifying contigs_final.fasta. Downstream analyses continue to use that assembly regardless of the reported decisions.

long_read_mode Reported decisions off (default) All contigs are marked keep with reason mode_off auto, include, exclude The decisions show which contigs the corresponding policy would retain or remove

Sample overrides affect the genus lists and discard_no_hit in this screen, but do not replace long_read_mode. If its policy would remove all contigs, the screen logs the result and the run continues.

Every hybrid run writes {sample}_final_contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv and {sample}_final_composition.tsv. Inspect both before acting on a decision: long-read assemblies may contain only a few contigs, and one removal can affect an entire chromosome or plasmid.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
Unless indicated otherwise, the files are under 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/.

File Contents and use contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv Contig genus assignments, retention decisions and reasons; the main audit file for the primary screen {sample}_composition.txt Each genus's share of assembly length and contig count, before filtering {sample}_kept_genus.txt Genus hint supplied to Bakta; empty if no retained contig has a genus assignment bestscore.blob.blobDB.table.txt BlobTools table supporting the primary decisions {sample}_blastout Primary BLAST results, in the 15-column format described below contigs.list Retained contig identifiers; not consumed by another rule contigs_sel.fasta Retained Illumina draft in hybrid mode assembly_decontam.fasta Retained assembly in nanopore mode, before optional polishing {sample}_final_blastout BLAST results for the final assembly; nanopore and hybrid only {sample}_final_contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv Hybrid final-assembly decisions; does not change the assembly {sample}_final_composition.tsv Composition report for the final hybrid assembly bestscore_final.blob_final.blobDB.table.txt BlobTools table for the final hybrid assembly

In illumina and contigs modes, retained sequences are written directly to 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta.

The mapping BAM and index, BlobTools JSON and coverage files, and Bowtie2 index files are temporary. The corresponding log is logs/select_contigs_{sample}.log.

docs.title: Genus composition
docs.text:
The composition report summarises all contigs in the BlobTools input table, including those subsequently removed. It is sorted by sequence-length share. For example:

GenusA: bp 0.46  contigs 0.22
GenusB: bp 0.31  contigs 0.38
GenusC: bp 0.14  contigs 0.24
GenusD: bp 0.09  contigs 0.16

bp is the fraction of total sequence length assigned to a genus; contigs is its fraction of the contig count. Here, GenusA has the largest length share and GenusB the largest contig count. The two auto_vote settings therefore select different genera.

Several substantial genus assignments can indicate a mixed culture or taxonomic assignment of one genome across related genera. The report alone does not distinguish these explanations. It is provided for inspection and is not an input to a later analysis step.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
The selector writes advisory warnings to logs/select_contigs_{sample}.log. These warnings do not alter the decisions.

Message begins Condition What to inspect WARNING: <N> genera each hold at least 5% of this assembly At least two genera each account for at least 5% of assembly length Possible mixed culture or assignment of one genome across several genera WARNING: decontamination is discarding <N>% of the assembly More than 20% of assembly length is removed Possible excessive filtering; compare removed contigs and assembly QC WARNING: <N> contigs from BlobTools table were not found in FASTA. Contig identifiers in the BlobTools table are absent from the FASTA Input-table mismatch or rewritten contig headers

The hybrid final-assembly screen logs to logs/screen_final_contigs_{sample}.log, where the removal warning reads WARNING: this policy would discard <N>% of the assembly … Nothing is removed.

These are review thresholds, not calibrated criteria for accepting or rejecting an isolate. For example, the composition above can produce both composition and removal warnings: a GenusA-only selection would remove 54% of the sequence before considering aliases or unclassified-contig handling.

CheckM completeness and contamination estimates help to interpret the first two warnings. A kept assembly that is incomplete but not contaminated suggests that genuine genome sequence was removed; one that is complete but heavily contaminated suggests that a second genome was kept. Read the estimates together with the contig decisions and the expected genome structure.

docs.title: When nothing survives
docs.text: If primary selection retains zero contigs, use the reason column in the audit file to distinguish a mismatched policy from a lack of usable assignments. The primary rule fails rather than writing an empty FASTA. The hybrid final-assembly screen is advisory and does not fail the run for this condition.

docs.title: Plasmid assignment can differ from the host
docs.text:
A plasmid can have close database matches in several genera. Its BlobTools genus assignment reflects the BLAST evidence and database representation; it is not a direct determination of the plasmid's current host. Consequently, auto filtering can remove a genuine plasmid assigned to a genus other than the selected genus.

In a BacFlux run on the complete assembly of Klebsiella pneumoniae ATCC BAA-2146 (mode: contigs; see the worked example), the 2,014 bp plasmid pMYS (NZ_CP006660.1) was removed by the default auto policy after assignment to Escherichia. Its single best hit was K. pneumoniae at 100% identity over the full sequence, but the summed bit scores favoured Escherichia: 58,709 compared with 16,253 for Klebsiella. These values are summed bit scores, not counts of database entries.

Genus-level filtering also cannot distinguish contaminants of the same genus from the intended isolate. Conversely, aliases or broad include lists can retain contaminants as well as genuine target sequence.

docs.title: Short-read guidance can propagate a filtering error
docs.text:
This additional risk applies only when parameters.hybrid.short_read_guidance: true.

  1. The primary screen removes an Illumina contig.
  2. Illumina reads mapping to that removed sequence are absent from the selected short-read reference.
  3. Filtlong uses that reference to score the Nanopore reads.
  4. Nanopore reads without short-read support can be removed, reducing or eliminating the sequence available to Flye.

A mistaken plasmid assignment can therefore affect the final hybrid assembly. This particular mechanism does not apply with short_read_guidance: false. Long-read quality and length filtering can independently remove plasmid reads; see Nanopore mode.

docs.title: Investigate a missing plasmid
docs.text:
1. Inspect discarded contigs in contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv, including short contigs that could represent plasmids. Compare their assigned genera with the expected host genus and the GTDB-Tk classification. NCBI and GTDB names need not be identical.
  2. Determine whether the sequence is absent from the assembly or is present but has no plasmid call in 06.plasmids/.
  3. In hybrid mode, check short_read_guidance and the final-assembly audit.
  4. Review long-read filtering and assembly results as well as the taxonomic filter. Absence from the assembly does not by itself identify the cause.

docs.title: Adjust the policy and reassess
docs.text:
Finding Possible change A genuine target contig was assigned to another genus Use include with both the host genus and the contig's assigned genus Taxonomic filtering is unsuitable for the current analysis Use off to retain all contigs, then assess contamination separately An unclassified contig was removed (reason discarded_no_hit) Set discard_no_hit: false and use exclude or off; under auto and include the contig is still removed One sample needs additional included genera Use include_genera_by_sample One sample needs a different policy or replacement genus list Use sample_overrides

Inspect the dry-run plan after changing the configuration, then rerun and compare the decision files, retained assembly and QC results. Changing long_read_mode changes only the hybrid audit decisions; it does not restore or remove sequence in the final assembly.

Implementation details and BLAST output format

The primary screen uses the following rules and software:

Rules Software or environment blast_contigs, blast_final_contigs BLAST+ 2.17.0 map_contigs, index_contigs in short-read modes Bowtie2 2.5.5, bowtie.yaml Long-read and contig self-alignment minimap2 2.31, minimap.yaml blob_json, blob_table BlobTools 1.1.1 select_contigs Standard-library Python in workflow/envs/python.yaml

The selector reads genus from column 22 of the BlobTools --rank all table. Rows with fewer than 22 fields are skipped; an empty genus field is read as no-hit. BlobTools uses:

blobtools view --input blob.blobDB.json --out bestscore \
  --taxrule bestsum --rank all --hits

The BLAST command has this form, with paths and sample names supplied by the workflow:

BLASTDB=/path/to/blast_db \
blastn -task megablast \
  -query contigs_filt.fasta \
  -db /path/to/blast_db/core_nt \
  -outfmt '6 qseqid staxids bitscore pident evalue length qlen slen qcovs qcovhsp sskingdoms scomnames sscinames sblastnames stitle' \
  -evalue 1e-5 -max_target_seqs 50 -max_hsps 5 \
  -num_threads {threads} -out {sample}_blastout

BLASTDB identifies the parent database directory; -db identifies the selected database within it. nodes.dmp and names.dmp must be available in the configured database directory.

Preserve the -outfmt columns when modifying the rule. The plasmid stage uses the final stitle column for its supplementary BLAST check. Changing its position makes that check fail without raising an error: every plasmid call is then reported as not verified by BLAST search.

The hybrid final screen uses map_final_contigs, blob_json_final, blob_table_final and screen_final_contigs.

docs.title: Prophages
docs.text:
Stage 07.phages predicts viral sequences, including phage contigs and integrated prophages, in contigs_final.fasta. CheckV then estimates the quality of the predicted sequences. The stage is available in all modes; assembly quality still affects detection and boundary resolution.

Select one of the two supported callers with phage.caller. CheckV v1.1.1 runs either way, to provide a shared assessment of completeness and host contamination.

phage:
  caller: virsorter2      # virsorter2 (default) | genomad (opt-in)

---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    F([contigs_final.fasta])

    G[genomad_end_to_end<br/>opt-in]
    V[viral_identification_virsorter2<br/>default]

    F --> G
    F --> V

    GV([07.phages/genomad/sample/<br/>..._summary/contigs_final_virus.fna])
    GP([..._plasmid_summary.tsv])
    VV([07.phages/virsorter/sample/<br/>final-viral-combined.fa])

    G --> GV
    G --> GP
    V --> VV

    GP --> S06[stage 06, plasmid concordance]

    Q[viral_quality<br/>CheckV]
    GV --> Q
    VV --> Q
    Q --> QS([07.phages/checkv/sample/<br/>quality_summary.tsv])

The two callers sit behind mutually exclusive guards, so only one set of rules is ever defined. The run prints which one it is at startup: Phage caller: virsorter2 (default). Plasmid stage: Platon-only (geNomad off).

Terms used on this page

HMM hidden Markov model — a statistical profile of a gene or protein family SOP standard operating procedure

docs.title: Choosing the caller
docs.text:
VirSorter2 2.2.4 geNomad 1.12.0 Status default opt-in Licence GPLv2 Berkeley Lab, academic / non-commercial use Finds viruses viruses and plasmids, in one run Database ~10 GB ~1.5 GB Also changes nothing else switches on the Platon + geNomad plasmid concordance in stage 06

VirSorter2 is the default because the whole default path — VirSorter2, Platon, CheckV — was chosen with their licences in view, and geNomad's did not fit. Licensing records what each licensor published and where it was read; read it before setting genomad.

Choosing geNomad also changes the plasmid stage, by design rather than as a side effect: one geNomad run produces both a virus FASTA and a plasmid summary, so opting in hands stage 06 a second, independent caller without a second run.

docs.title: VirSorter2
docs.text:
Rules virsorter2_db (or virsorter2_db_local) and viral_identification_virsorter2.

VirSorter2 scores contigs against curated viral HMM groups. BacFlux uses the settings from the VirSorter2 SOP:

Setting Value Why --include-groups dsDNAphage,NCLDV,RNA,ssDNA,lavidaviridae the five groups the SOP screens for --min-score 0.5 deliberately loose, for sensitivity — CheckV downstream is what grades the result --keep-original-seq on keeps the original sequence of circular and near-fully-viral contigs instead of VirSorter2's trimmed version, so CheckV sees the real contig In contigs_final.fasta + the VirSorter2 database Out 07.phages/virsorter/{sample}/ — key file final-viral-combined.fa Next CheckV

The ~10 GB database is fetched once by virsorter setup. If you already hold a copy — the directory that command produced, containing hmm/, group/, rbs/ and Done_all_setup — point directories.vs2_db at it and nothing is downloaded. BacFlux then builds a symlink view of it rather than reading it in place, because Snakemake wipes a directory() output before re-running its rule, and that must never happen to a database someone else shares.

Why envs/virsorter.yaml lists so many packages

VirSorter2 is itself a Snakemake workflow, and left alone it builds a second conda environment at run time and does its real work inside that. That nesting is what broke every phage run before v2.0.0: an old transitive mamba against a modern conda, failing with No module named 'conda._vendor.auxlib'.

BacFlux switches the nesting off — virsorter setup --skip-deps-install, virsorter run --use-conda-off, and the environment's own bin put first on PATH — which means every tool VirSorter2's internal rules call must already be in our environment. The bioconda virsorter package does not bring them: with virsorter alone, screed, hmmer, prodigal, last, pandas, scikit-learn, numpy, seaborn, imbalanced-learn and ncbi-genome-download were all absent and the run died at the first internal rule on No module named 'screed'. So envs/virsorter.yaml carries a copy of VirSorter2's own internal dependency list, pins included — its classifier ships as a pickled scikit-learn 0.22.1 model, so the pins matter. If VirSorter2 is ever unpinned from 2.2.4, that list has to be re-synced against the envs/vs2.yaml inside the package.

docs.title: geNomad
docs.text:
Rules genomad_db (or genomad_db_local) and genomad_end_to_end, defined only when phage.caller: genomad.

geNomad classifies each contig from its gene content against a marker-profile database, and reports viruses and plasmids in the same run. BacFlux uses the default presets — neither --conservative nor --relaxed — which is the combination CheckV is normally paired with, and --cleanup to delete the intermediates.

In contigs_final.fasta + the geNomad database Out 07.phages/genomad/{sample}/contigs_final_summary/ — contigs_final_virus.fna and contigs_final_plasmid_summary.tsv Next CheckV (virus FASTA) and the plasmid concordance in stage 06 (plasmid summary)

Database source when using geNomad

genomad download-database is hard-coded to portal.nersc.gov — the same host whose outages forced the CheckV database onto a Zenodo mirror — and it has no --url option, so a mirror cannot be substituted the way links.checkv_link is. It fails as URLError: [Errno 113] No route to host when that host is down.

BacFlux ships links.genomad_link pointing at the copy geNomad's own authors published on Zenodo (record 14886553, database v1.9), with links.genomad_md5 beside it; a checksum mismatch stops the run rather than extracting a truncated archive. Change one and you must change the other. Better still, set directories.genomad_db to a copy you already hold — the inner genomad_db/ directory, the one holding version.txt and genomad_db.dbtype, not its parent.

A local geNomad database is checked at parse time, before any job starts, because both ways it can fail are slow and confusing to diagnose mid-run:

  • Partly readable. On a shared copy it is easy for a few small files, version.txt among them, to end up mode 0640 while the large data files beside them are world-readable. os.path.exists() is true for a file you may stat but not read, so BacFlux tests real read access on every file and names the offenders.
  • Too old for the installed geNomad. geNomad parses genomad_marker_metadata.tsv by position from the end of each row, so a database with one fewer trailing column shifts every field and dies minutes in on invalid literal for int() — a marker accession being read as a count. BacFlux checks for the PREVIOUS_MARKER_ACCESSION column instead of a version number, because that column's absence is the actual cause.

docs.title: CheckV
docs.text:
Rule viral_quality, plus checkv_db or checkv_db_local.

CheckV estimates how complete each predicted viral sequence is, flags host sequence left on the ends of proviruses, and trims it. The same checkv end_to_end command grades either caller's output, so one rule serves both paths — the caller's directory is chosen at startup and the rule itself never knows which one it got.

In whichever caller's virus FASTA, plus the CheckV database Out 07.phages/checkv/{sample}/ — key file quality_summary.tsv Next this is the end of the stage; the CheckV directory is what rule all asks for, and asking for it is what pulls in whichever caller ran

quality_summary.tsv is the file to read: one row per predicted viral sequence, with checkv_quality, completeness, contamination, viral and host gene counts, and CheckV's own warnings. Under VirSorter2, treat a low-completeness, high-host-gene row as what the loose 0.5 cutoff was expected to produce — the caller is deliberately sensitive.

No predicted viral sequences

checkv end_to_end errors on an empty input, and a virus-free genome is a perfectly normal result. So the rule tests the caller's FASTA first: if it holds no sequences, it writes a header-only quality_summary.tsv and skips CheckV. A header-only table therefore means either that the caller returned no viral sequences, or that CheckV exited with an error and the run continued; logs/viral_quality_{sample}.log says which. Neither shows that the genome carries no prophage.

The shipped default is checkv-db-v1.5, fetched from an unmodified Zenodo mirror (links.checkv_link) with its .sha256 checked, or from CheckV's own downloader when that link is cleared. Either way it lands in 07.phages/checkv_db/ and the rule finds the versioned folder inside it at run time, so the two routes are interchangeable.

If you hold a copy already, set directories.checkv_db to the parent directory holding the versioned folder. BacFlux symlinks the large files rather than copying them, but rebuilds the DIAMOND index with this workflow's own DIAMOND: index formats are versioned, and an index built by another site's DIAMOND makes CheckV fail deep into the completeness stage with DIAMOND task failed. That rebuild costs about 950 MB against roughly 6.4 GB for a full copy.

docs.title: What this stage does and does not feed
docs.text: The prophage calls are a deliverable in their own right. A prophage is a mobile element, so the mobilome module counts this stage as part of its subject — but not as an input: no rule in stage 08 opens a file under 07.phages/. Stage 08 does consume the plasmid stage, and opting in to geNomad changes what that stage hands it, because the concordance table is built here.

docs.title: What to check afterwards
docs.text:
• 07.phages/checkv/{sample}/quality_summary.tsv — the graded calls, or a header-only file when nothing was called.
  • 07.phages/virsorter/{sample}/final-viral-combined.fa or 07.phages/genomad/{sample}/contigs_final_summary/contigs_final_virus.fna — what the caller proposed before CheckV.
  • logs/viral_quality_{sample}.log — CheckV's own output, or the "no viral sequences called" line.
  • logs/virsorter2_db.log, logs/genomad_db.log, logs/checkv_db.log — the one-off database steps; the geNomad and CheckV logs record the checksum result. When you supplied the database yourself, the log is the _local variant of the same name.

docs.title: Plasmids
docs.text:
Stage 06.plasmids predicts plasmid contigs in contigs_final.fasta with Platon. It runs in all modes. An optional geNomad result provides an additional classification, and a supplementary BLAST lookup is reported alongside the calls. Assembly structure and the available evidence affect interpretation.

Platon v1.8 is the caller and always runs. geNomad v1.12.0 is an optional second opinion: it is switched on from the phage stage, not from here, because one geNomad run calls viruses and plasmids together.

---
config:
  themeVariables:
    fontSize: 14px
  flowchart:
    nodeSpacing: 35
    rankSpacing: 35
---
flowchart TD
    F([contigs_final.fasta]) --> P[plasmid_search<br/>Platon]
    P --> VP([06.plasmids/sample/platon/<br/>verified_plasmids.txt])
    GN([07.phages/genomad/sample/<br/>..._plasmid_summary.tsv<br/>only when geNomad is opted in])
    VP --> PC[plasmid_concordance]
    GN --> PC
    PC --> OUT([sample_plasmid_concordance.tsv])

Which of the two end files is the deliverable depends on one config key:

phage.caller Plasmid deliverable geNomad virsorter2 (default) 06.plasmids/{sample}/platon/verified_plasmids.txt never runs genomad (opt-in) 06.plasmids/{sample}/{sample}_plasmid_concordance.tsv runs once per sample, in stage 07

Platon runs either way. See Prophages for the caller choice itself.

Terms used on this page

FDR false discovery rate, the expected share of calls at a given score that are wrong

docs.title: Platon
docs.text:
Rule plasmid_search.

Platon scores every contig on its protein content. Each protein family carries a replicon-distribution score (RDS) — how much more often that family is seen on a plasmid than on a chromosome — and the contig's summed score decides the call. It needs the Platon database, set as directories.platon_db; see Reference databases.

In contigs_final.fasta, plus a BLAST table computed over those same contigs (which one depends on the mode — see below) Out 06.plasmids/{sample}/platon/ — contigs_final.tsv, contigs_final.plasmid.fasta, contigs_final.chromosome.fasta, verified_plasmids.txt Next the concordance rule (when geNomad is on), and the mobilome module's replicon table (when it is on)

Platon's own output files are named after the input, which is always contigs_final.fasta, so the stem is contigs_final in every mode.

docs.title: The BLAST line beside each call
docs.text:
For every contig Platon calls a plasmid, the rule takes that contig's first line in the BLAST table and asks — case-insensitively — whether it mentions "plasmid". In practice that is the subject title, which is why Decontamination warns against reordering the -outfmt columns. The answer is one line per contig in verified_plasmids.txt:

sample01: contig_3 is a plasmid.
sample01: contig_9 was not verified by BLAST search.

A genome Platon called no plasmid on gets a single Platon found no plasmid in sample … line instead. That is a result, not an error.

The BLAST line is an annotation, never a filter — nothing is dropped on the strength of it. Both signals can be fooled by the same thing: a mobile element sitting on a genuinely chromosomal contig pushes Platon's score and that contig's best nt hit in the same wrong direction, so agreement here is weaker evidence than it looks.

Which BLAST table is used differs by mode, and is resolved once at startup:

Mode Table Why illumina, contigs the decontamination screen's own BLAST output the screen already ran on this exact contig set nanopore, hybrid a second megablast over contigs_final.fasta (rule blast_final_contigs) nothing guarantees Medaka preserves contig headers, and the hybrid screen runs on the Illumina draft, whose SPAdes NODE_… names can never match Flye's contig_… names

The lookup is by contig ID, so the wrong table would report every plasmid as "not verified by BLAST search" — silently, with no error. That is the reason it is resolved centrally rather than per rule.

An almost-empty Platon directory is a normal result, not a failure

Platon refuses to classify a contig longer than 500 kb (MAX_CONTIG_LENGTH in Platon's own source). A closed chromosome is therefore in neither the plasmid nor the chromosome FASTA — it was never assessed. On a complete Nanopore or hybrid assembly this is the usual case, and the per-contig table can legitimately be header-only.

A real Platon crash looks different: the rule traps the exit status and writes one line, {sample}: Platon exited with status N; see the log., into verified_plasmids.txt instead of killing the sample. That line is the only reliable signal that Platon failed, and both downstream readers key on it.

docs.title: geNomad as a second opinion
docs.text:
Rule plasmid_concordance, defined only when phage.caller: genomad.

geNomad classifies contigs from gene content against its own marker set — a different method with different failure modes — so agreement with Platon provides additional support. The workflow's agreement labels are heuristic confidence categories, not calibrated probabilities, and the two methods can still share sources of error. geNomad is licensed by Berkeley Lab for academic / non-commercial use; the terms of every tool are listed under Licensing.

The rule joins four files into one table: Platon's per-contig table, Platon's chromosome FASTA, verified_plasmids.txt, and geNomad's plasmid summary from stage 07. One row per plasmid candidate — the union of the two tools' plasmid calls. Contigs both tools agree are chromosome are left out.

Column Holds sample, contig the join keys platon_call plasmid | chromosome | not_called | not_assessed platon_rds Platon's replicon-distribution score, or NA platon_blast_hit hit | no_hit | NA — the supplementary BLAST line above genomad_call plasmid | absent genomad_score, genomad_fdr geNomad's plasmid score, and its FDR when calibration ran (usually NA) agreement which tools called it confidence high | medium | low, from agreement alone

Agreement drives the tier, and nothing is discarded — a disagreement is flagged and kept, so the table is its own audit trail:

Platon geNomad agreement confidence plasmid plasmid both high plasmid — platon_only medium not called plasmid genomad_only medium chromosome plasmid conflict low crashed anything platon_unavailable low

Three rows from the Klebsiella pneumoniae ATCC BAA-2146 positive control (sample and genomad_fdr not shown). The two tools agree on all three plasmid contigs that reached this stage — the genome's fourth plasmid never did, because decontamination had already removed it (see below):

contig          platon_call  platon_rds  platon_blast_hit  genomad_call  genomad_score  agreement  confidence
NZ_CP006661.1   plasmid      31.8        hit               plasmid       0.9925         both       high
NZ_CP006662.2   plasmid      20.1        hit               plasmid       0.9937         both       high
NZ_CP006663.1   plasmid      27.1        hit               plasmid       0.9943         both       high

The comparison is not symmetric yet

The rule reads only geNomad's plasmid summary, which lists positive calls. So genomad_call: absent means "geNomad did not call this a plasmid" and cannot distinguish "it actively called it chromosome" from "it never scored it". The forward clash — Platon chromosome against geNomad plasmid — is flagged conflict / low. The reverse case, Platon plasmid against geNomad silence, is reported platon_only / medium rather than as a conflict. Nothing is hidden either way; only that one tier label is conservative.

If both tools called plasmids but none of their contig IDs match, the script says so in the log. The join has broken — a header not trimmed to its first token somewhere upstream — and every genuine both / high has split into two single-tool medium rows.

docs.title: What the mobility ladder takes from here
docs.text:
When the mobilome module is on, it reads this stage rather than re-detecting anything. Platon already answers both questions the top of the ladder needs: whether a contig is a plasmid at all, and whether that plasmid carries the machinery to move itself, from its own # Conjugation, # Mobilization and # OriT counts.

Platon counts Plasmid mobility Ladder conjugation genes present conjugative tier 6 — predicted self-transmissible no conjugation, but a relaxase or an oriT mobilisable tier 5 — needs a helper neither non-mobilisable —

Conjugation is tested first because a relaxase is part of a conjugative system, not an alternative to one. Contigs Platon skipped for length are called chromosome only at 2 Mb and above; between 500 kb and 2 Mb the replicon is reported unknown, because megaplasmids of that size exist. When geNomad is on, the concordance table is passed in as well, so a plasmid Platon missed does not silently become "chromosomal, intrinsic candidate".

docs.title: Before you conclude a plasmid is absent
docs.text:
Decontamination can remove a small plasmid before this stage sees it

The auto selector keeps contigs whose assigned genus matches the sample's dominant genus. A genuine plasmid can be discarded when its database matches produce a genus assignment different from the selected host genus — the measured case is the 2,014 bp plasmid pMYS of the control genome above, dropped as Escherichia (Decontamination). Check 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv before trusting an absence. In hybrid mode with short-read guidance on there is a second route, worse than the first: a contig dropped there takes its long reads with it, so the sequence is missing from the assembly and not merely from the plasmid call (Route 2).

Small plasmids are also lost upstream of that, at read filtering and assembly. The settings that decide it are covered on Nanopore mode.

docs.title: What to check afterwards
docs.text:
• 06.plasmids/{sample}/platon/verified_plasmids.txt — the per-contig call and its BLAST line, or the one-line Platon failure message.
  • 06.plasmids/{sample}/{sample}_plasmid_concordance.tsv — when geNomad is on, the tiered table, including every flagged conflict.
  • logs/plasmid_search_{sample}.log — Platon's own verbose output.
  • logs/plasmid_concordance_{sample}.log — the join summary: candidate contigs, how many scored both, how many conflicts, and how many geNomad IDs matched a Platon contig ID.

docs.title: Taxonomy
docs.text:
Stage 03.taxonomy classifies the assembly with GTDB-Tk 2.7.2 and the GTDB R232 reference. Use the reported lineage, ANI evidence and classification notes together when assessing the isolate's identity.

classify_wf finds the ~120 bacterial marker proteins in the genome, aligns them and places them on the Genome Taxonomy Database reference tree, then refines the call with skani ANI comparisons against the closest reference genomes. The answer is a full lineage from domain to species with the ANI evidence behind it.

That matters for strain assessment: whether an AMR gene found later reads as intrinsic or acquired depends on having the species right; see the mobility ladder.

Terms used on this page

ANI average nucleotide identity, the percentage identity between two genomes over the sequence they share AMR antimicrobial resistance

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
Rule taxonomic_assignment, workflow/rules/shared/30_taxonomy.smk.

GTDBTK_DATA_PATH=/path/to/release232 \
gtdbtk classify_wf -x fasta \
  --genome_dir 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/genomes \
  --out_dir 03.taxonomy/{sample} \
  --cpus {threads} --pplacer_cpus {threads}

In: the staged genome directory that stage_qc_genomes filled — this sample's one genome, or two in hybrid mode, named after their bin ids.

Out: 03.taxonomy/{sample}/, a directory, because GTDB-Tk names the files inside it. The one to read is the summary TSV, classify/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv. GTDB-Tk has moved that file between releases, so the report stage looks inside classify/ first and then at the top level.

Consumed by: MultiQC, which reads the summary; and — only when the mobilome module is on — the rule that translates the species call into an AMRFinderPlus --organism name, which is what unlocks point-mutation detection. GTDB and NCBI do not use the same species names, so that translation goes through a curated lookup table generated per GTDB release; an unmapped species degrades silently to no --organism at all, which is the common case for environmental isolates. How the table is built and used is on the AMR page.

The rule also takes CheckM's statistics file as an input. That is a scheduling edge, not a data dependency: GTDB-Tk reads only the genome directory. Both tools run pplacer and each can use tens of GB, so on a large machine dropping the edge would let them run concurrently on the same sample and risk an out-of-memory kill. Keeping it costs nothing and preserves the ordering.

docs.title: Hybrid: one run, two rows
docs.text:
A hybrid sample stages two genomes, and one classify_wf run classifies both. The summary comes back with two rows keyed by the staged basenames, {sample}_illumina and {sample}_ont. They need no separate output files: the report rewrites the keys into taxonomy Illumina | {sample} and taxonomy ONT | {sample}, and 02.assembly/{sample}/eval/{sample}_qc_genomes.tsv records which of the two is the delivered genome.

Investigate disagreement between the hybrid classifications. Compare assembly quality, retained sequences and reference-match evidence; differences can reflect the assemblies, filtering or the evidence available to the classifier.

docs.title: GTDB names are not NCBI names
docs.text:
GTDB splits genera and gives them a letter suffix (Pseudomonas_E), and it uses placeholder species names for lineages with no published name (sp024807945). That is a property of GTDB, not a fault — it is what makes the taxonomy consistent with genome phylogeny.

It does mean the name you get here will not always match a name in NCBI-derived resources. Where BacFlux needs to cross that gap it does so explicitly, with a curated lookup, rather than assuming the two vocabularies agree.

docs.title: Version and database are pinned together
docs.text:
GTDB-Tk hard-pins itself to one compatible reference release, in its own COMPATIBLE_REF_DATA_VERSIONS. Version 2.6.1 accepted only r220 and r226, so GTDB R232 requires 2.7.0 or later; the environment pins 2.7.2. There is no in-place upgrade from an older release directory — download R232 and point directories.gtdbtk_db at it. Sizes and the download recipe are in Reference databases.

The version bump also changed how the skani reference is laid out. Under R226 the release shipped a raw skani reference and GTDB-Tk built its own sketch cache on first use. From R232 the release ships that sketch pre-built, which is what roughly halves the space GTDB-Tk needs — the R232 package extracts to 94 GB and no longer builds a ~57 GB sketch cache beside it. classify_wf reads it straight out of {gtdbtk_db}/skani/, and the --skani_sketch_dir flag no longer exists in the command line at all, so there is nothing left for the rule to build or point at.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
--cpus and --pplacer_cpus are both set to min(resources.threads, 24) — one parameter, and --cores caps what Snakemake grants on top of it. pplacer's memory scales with its thread count and can reach tens of GB, which is why the cap exists. Thread count changes runtime and memory use, not any classification setting. Classifications from different runs are comparable only with the same GTDB-Tk version and reference release.

This is the single most expensive step in a BacFlux run, which is also why a hybrid sample is classified in one invocation rather than two: classify_wf loads the reference tree and the skani sketches on every call.

docs.title: What to check afterwards
docs.text:
• 03.taxonomy/{sample}/classify/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv — the lineage, the closest reference genome and its ANI. A species-level call needs the ANI to clear GTDB's threshold; below it, the row stops at genus.
  • The genus here against {sample}_composition.txt from decontamination. A mismatch warrants review of the per-contig assignments in 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants/contig_taxonomy_decisions.tsv and of the GTDB-Tk call. Decontamination uses NCBI taxonomy and GTDB-Tk uses GTDB names, so part of a mismatch can be nomenclature alone.
  • 09.report/multiqc_report.html — the classification for the whole batch on one page.

docs.title: Choosing a mode
docs.text:
Select mode according to the available input: Illumina paired-end reads, Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) reads, both read types from the same isolate, or an existing assembly. The modes share analysis rules but differ in assembly processing and in the read-dependent analyses they can perform.

Terms used on this page

QC quality control AMR antimicrobial resistance IS insertion sequence — the smallest mobile element, carrying only the genes it needs to move DAG directed acyclic graph — the job graph Snakemake plans a run from mode You have File names BacFlux looks for Input key illumina Illumina paired-end reads {sample}_R1.<ext> and {sample}_R2.<ext> input.illumina_dir nanopore ONT long reads {sample}_ont.<ext> input.nanopore_dir hybrid Both, for the same isolates both of the above both directories contigs A finished assembly and no reads {sample}.<fasta\|fa\|fna> input.contigs_dir

<ext> for reads is one of fastq, fq, fastq.gz, fq.gz, and every sample in one batch must share the same one — a directory holding both .fastq and .fastq.gz stops the run and lists what it found. The same applies to the FASTA extension in contigs mode. Sample names may contain underscores and dots; spaces and the characters * # @ % ^ / ! ? & : ; | < > are rejected.

docs.title: Configure the input mode
docs.text:
Two keys in config/config.yaml pick the front end: mode, and the input directory or directories that mode reads. The input directories it does not read can stay empty — the output directory and the database paths under directories: are needed whichever mode you pick.

mode: illumina                 # illumina | nanopore | hybrid | contigs

input:
  illumina_dir: "/data/run1/illumina"
  nanopore_dir: ""
  contigs_dir:  ""

Both are checked before any job starts, so a mistake costs you seconds rather than hours. Write mode: ilumina — one l short — and the run stops with:

config.mode must be one of illumina | nanopore | hybrid | contigs (got: 'ilumina')

A valid run echoes the mode and every sample it found, so the batch can be confirmed from the top of the log:

Mode: illumina — Genomic analysis of bacterial Illumina reads.
Sample isolate_01 will be processed.
Sample isolate_02 will be processed.

The mode can be overridden for a single run with --config mode=contigs, but the matching input.*_dir almost always has to change with it, so editing the file is usually simpler.

docs.title: Mode-specific input processing
docs.text:
illumina nanopore hybrid contigs Read QC PhiX removal with Bowtie2, then fastp NanoPlot before and after, Filtlong both of those none Assembler SPAdes --isolate, k chosen from read length Flye Flye, over the ONT reads none After assembly keep contigs ≥ 500 bp and ≥ 2× coverage dnaapler reorientation, then Medaka (optional — parameters.<mode>.medaka_model: false skips it) dnaapler and Medaka as in nanopore, then Polypolish correction with the Illumina reads SPAdes-style headers: the same 500 bp / 2× filter, headers left as they are. Any other header: trimmed to its first whitespace token, nothing filtered Contamination screen SPAdes draft; retained contigs form the final assembly Reoriented assembly, before optional Medaka polishing Primary filter on the Illumina draft; optional short-read guidance for Filtlong; advisory screen of the final assembly Supplied contigs; retained contigs form the final assembly Delivered genome the screened SPAdes contigs the Flye assembly, reoriented, screened and polished the ONT assembly corrected by Polypolish the screened input contigs Also produced — — the Illumina draft, kept as a comparator, and a Snippy comparison of the two —

Hybrid mode assembles the Illumina reads with SPAdes and the Nanopore reads with Flye, so it requires more computation than either single-technology mode. Reads mapping to the decontaminated Illumina draft support Polypolish correction. They also guide Filtlong when parameters.hybrid.short_read_guidance: true; this option is disabled by default. The final assembly receives a separate advisory taxonomic screen that reports decisions without removing contigs.

docs.title: Everything after the assembly is shared
docs.text:
Each front end ends by writing one file, contigs_final.fasta, and from there the shared analysis stages assess the final assembly: assembly QC, completeness and contamination, taxonomic placement, annotation, AMR and virulence screening, plasmids, prophages, the optional mobilome module, and one MultiQC report. See Output files for what each stage writes.

Decontamination is the one shared step that is not downstream of that file. It is the same screening code in every mode, but it sits inside the front end, at the different points the table above gives — which is why in illumina and contigs its output is contigs_final.fasta. See Decontamination.

docs.title: What the mode still decides downstream
docs.text:
A few shared steps need something a given mode does not have. They are gated on the capability — short reads, long reads, any reads — rather than on the mode name, and when the capability is absent the rule is not defined, so it does not appear in the DAG and nothing waits for it.

Shared step Needs illumina nanopore hybrid contigs CARD read mapping (05.amr/mapping) short reads ✓ — ✓ — Qualimap mapping evaluation any reads ✓ ✓ ✓ — Coverage that carries information for BlobTools any reads ✓ ✓ ✓ — Circular-replicon table handed to Bakta Flye's topology calls — ✓ ✓ — Second BLAST of the final assembly, for the plasmid stage long reads — ✓ ✓ — IS copy number from reads (mobilome, optional) short reads ✓ — ✓ — Two genomes through QC and taxonomy, plus the Snippy comparison both technologies — — ✓ —

The same table appears on Modes, which is where it is maintained. Four consequences worth knowing before you choose:

  • contigs mode cannot separate contaminants by coverage. BlobTools needs a BAM, and with no reads the contigs are mapped against themselves, which gives a self-alignment coverage value rather than independent sequencing depth. Taxonomic evidence determines contig selection in all modes. See Decontamination.
  • nanopore and contigs lose the read-based AMR analysis. Mapping reads to CARD side-steps the assembly, so a resistance gene present in several copies, or sitting on a repeat that broke the contig, can be visible in the reads and absent from the assembly. The separate CARD mapping analysis requires Illumina reads and is unavailable in these two modes. ABRicate screening of the contigs still runs in every mode. See Antimicrobial resistance.
  • Only the long-read modes know that a contig is circular. Flye reports it per contig, and Bakta is told through --replicons, which lets the gene caller call a gene that runs across the origin — often dnaA itself. In illumina and contigs mode Bakta treats every sequence as linear.
  • The mobilome module is available in all four modes, with confidence affected by assembly structure. On a fragmented assembly the located insertion-sequence count is a floor rather than a count, because the elements being detected are a leading cause of the contig breaks. Every call therefore carries its distance to the contig end, and anything spanning contigs is capped at low confidence. In the short-read modes, and only when an ISOSDB source is configured, read-based analysis provides an additional copy-number estimate. See Draft assemblies.

docs.title: Input-mode errors
docs.text:
Usually it stops within seconds, because the four filename conventions do not overlap. Pointing illumina at a directory of {sample}_ont.fastq.gz:

[BacFlux] No suitable illumina input files found.

and hybrid at two directories that do not describe the same isolates:

[BacFlux] hybrid mode needs Illumina and ONT reads for every sample.
Missing ONT files for the following samples:
  - isolate_03

An unset or non-existent input directory is caught in the same pass:

[BacFlux] mode=nanopore requires 'input.nanopore_dir' to be set in the config.

Each of these stops Snakemake with exit status 1, before any job has started.

Two cases that do not stop the run

illumina on a dataset that also has long reads. It runs to the end and quietly ignores nanopore_dir. There is nothing to detect: the Illumina half is a valid illumina run. If you meant to use both, the mode is hybrid.

contigs on an assembly whose headers are not SPAdes-style. No length filter and no coverage filter are applied — only the headers are trimmed to their first whitespace token, which every later step keys on. That is deliberate, because the length and coverage of each contig are read out of the SPAdes header and inventing them for another assembler would silently delete real sequence. But it means the only contigs that can leave the assembly are the ones the contamination screen drops. The rule logs which branch it took.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Reads from one instrument — use that instrument's mode. hybrid adds nothing to a dataset with only one technology.
  • Both technologies for the same isolates — hybrid, and give it two directories in which every isolate appears in both. A sample present in only one of them stops the run rather than being silently dropped, so filter the directories to the complete isolates first.
  • Assembly of repetitive regions or assessment of replicon topology — use nanopore or hybrid when suitable long reads are available. These modes use Flye topology calls to provide circular-replicon information to Bakta. Long reads do not guarantee a complete or correctly resolved assembly.
  • A genome from a collaborator, a database, or an earlier assembly — contigs. It runs every analysis stage, but cannot re-examine evidence that only exists in reads.
  • Something already analysed with a workflow older than v2.0.0 — these four modes replace the separate repositories that used to do these jobs. See Coming from v1.

docs.title: Reference databases
docs.text:
BacFlux requires reference databases in addition to its conda environments. Five core databases must be prepared before an analysis. Other databases are downloaded as required by the selected analyses, or can be supplied through local paths.

Database group Preparation Bakta, NCBI nucleotide database, eggNOG, GTDB and Platon Download the compatible releases and set the five required directories.*_db paths PhiX, CARD, dbCAN, antiSMASH, CheckV and the selected phage caller's database Downloaded by the workflow when needed Existing local copies of CheckV, VirSorter2, antiSMASH, dbCAN, CARD or geNomad Set the corresponding optional path to skip its download Optional mobilome layers Configure each required source; see Optional layers

Nothing is written back into a database you supply. BacFlux reads your copy through a local symlink view and never modifies, moves or deletes it.

Terms used on this page

GTDB Genome Taxonomy Database, the reference used for taxonomic placement

docs.title: The five you download
docs.text:
Config key Database Database version Size on disk directories.bakta_db Bakta v6.0 3.9 GB light, 84 GB full directories.blast_db NCBI core_nt (or nt_prok) with the taxonomy files — ~300 GB directories.eggnog_db eggNOG diamond database v5.0.2 ~50 GB directories.gtdbtk_db GTDB R232 94 GB extracted directories.platon_db Platon v1.5.0 2.8 GB

Two of those versions are requirements. Bakta 1.12.1 refuses a v5.x database, and GTDB-Tk 2.7.2 pins itself to one GTDB release and rejects R226 or older. There is no in-place upgrade for either.

Two further compatibility requirements concern eggNOG and Platon. The eggNOG release is fixed by the pinned eggnog-mapper 2.1.15, which builds its own download URL from __DB_VERSION__ in the installed release, so the database cannot drift away from the tool. And the Platon database is versioned separately from Platon itself: v1.5.0 is current for every Platon from 1.5.0 onwards, including the 1.8 pinned here, so the database number trailing the tool number is expected.

docs.title: Bakta
docs.text:
# full database (recommended)
wget -c https://zenodo.org/records/14916843/files/db.tar.xz
tar -xJf db.tar.xz && rm db.tar.xz

# or the light version
wget -c https://zenodo.org/records/14916843/files/db-light.tar.xz
tar -xJf db-light.tar.xz && rm db-light.tar.xz

Note the archives are .tar.xz (hence -xJf), not .tar.gz as in earlier releases.

If AMRFinderPlus errors on its database, refresh it in place

The Bakta archive ships an AMRFinderPlus database alongside the annotation data, and the two can fall out of step with the AMRFinderPlus binary in the Bakta conda environment. The symptom is a database error from AMRFinderPlus, not a wrong result — most often when the mobilome module runs, since that is what reads it.

Activate the Bakta conda environment and point the update at your Bakta database directory:

amrfinder_update --force_update --database db/amrfinderplus-db/

BacFlux never does this for you. The workflow only ever reads {bakta_db}/amrfinderplus-db/latest; it does not check the database's age and does not refresh it, so a stale copy stays stale until you run the command above.

The mobilome module reuses the AMRFinderPlus database

The module reads AMRFinderPlus data from {bakta_db}/amrfinderplus-db/. CONJscan models are downloaded separately, and additional data sources are needed for the optional layers described below.

docs.title: NCBI core nt
docs.text:
# NCBI's own downloader. It ships with BLAST+, so it is already in the blast
# environment; --decompress unpacks each volume as it arrives, and every transfer
# is checked against the .md5 NCBI publishes beside it.
update_blastdb.pl --decompress --num_threads 4 core_nt      # or nt_prok

# taxonomy: BlobTools reads nodes.dmp and names.dmp from this same directory
wget -c 'https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/taxonomy/taxdump.tar.gz' && tar -zxf taxdump.tar.gz
wget -c 'https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/blast/db/taxdb.tar.gz'       && tar -zxf taxdb.tar.gz
wget -c 'https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/taxonomy/accession2taxid/nucl_gb.accession2taxid.gz'
gunzip nucl_gb.accession2taxid.gz

Use the HTTPS download recipe

The commands above use HTTPS and update_blastdb.pl. The downloader resolves the database volume list and checks the published MD5 values, so no release-specific list of volumes has to be maintained. NCBI no longer serves rsync: rsync://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov answers Connection refused (checked in October 2026), so recipes built on it fail.

nodes.dmp and names.dmp must sit in the same directory as the BLAST volumes. parameters.nt_version chooses which subfolder is searched: core_nt (default) or nt_prok.

docs.title: eggNOG
docs.text:
conda create -n eggnog-mapper eggnog-mapper=2.1.15
conda activate eggnog-mapper
mkdir /data/eggnog_db
download_eggnog_data.py --data_dir /data/eggnog_db -y

docs.title: GTDB
docs.text:
wget -c https://data.gtdb.ecogenomic.org/releases/release232/232.0/auxillary_files/gtdbtk_package/full_package/gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz
tar xzf gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz && rm gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz

The archive is ~61 GB. Point gtdbtk_db at the release232 directory itself. GTDB-Tk 2.7.x reads a pre-sketched skani database that GTDB now ships inside the release, so unlike 2.6.x it neither builds nor needs space for its own ~57 GB sketch cache.

If the single 61 GB archive is awkward on your connection, GTDB also publishes it split into 12 parts, which can be pulled in parallel and joined:

# split package (alternative) — r232 has 12 parts, aa..al
base_url="https://data.gtdb.ecogenomic.org/releases/release232/232.0/auxillary_files/gtdbtk_package/split_package/gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz.part_"
suffixes=(aa ab ac ad ae af ag ah ai aj ak al)
printf "%s\n" "${suffixes[@]}" | xargs -n 1 -P 12 -I {} wget -c "${base_url}{}"

cat gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz.part_* > gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz
tar xzf gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz
rm gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz gtdbtk_r232_data.tar.gz.part_*

The part count is release-specific — R226 had 14 (aa..an). cat joins whatever matches the glob without complaint, so a part that failed to download produces a corrupt archive rather than an error: check you have all 12 before joining.

docs.title: Platon
docs.text:
wget https://zenodo.org/record/4066768/files/db.tar.gz
tar -xzf db.tar.gz && rm db.tar.gz

docs.title: What the workflow fetches for itself
docs.text:
These land under output_dir and are shared by every sample in the run. Reuse the same output directory across runs of a project and they are downloaded once.

Database Where it lands Link key Read in PhiX 01.reads/phix/ (kept: the genome, and the Bowtie2 index the first run builds from it, about 8 MB) links.phix_link illumina, hybrid — required CARD 05.amr/card_db/ (kept, about 50 MB) links.card_link illumina, hybrid — required dbCAN 04.annotation/dbcan/<version>/ links.dbcan_link all antiSMASH 04.annotation/antismash/databases/ — (its own downloader) all CheckV 07.phages/checkv_db/ links.checkv_link all VirSorter2 07.phages/vs2_db/ — (virsorter setup) unless phage.caller: genomad geNomad 07.phages/genomad_db/ links.genomad_link + genomad_md5 only when phage.caller: genomad

phix_link and card_link ship empty and are required in the two modes that have short reads. An unset one stops the run at parse time, naming the key.

Two defaults point at Zenodo mirrors rather than the publisher's own host: CheckV's official database lives on portal.nersc.gov, as does geNomad's downloader, and NERSC is often unreachable, sometimes for a whole day. The CheckV default is an unmodified copy of the official archive, and the geNomad default is the Zenodo record published by geNomad's own authors. Change links.genomad_md5 whenever you change links.genomad_link: a mismatch stops rule genomad_db before the archive is extracted.

The dbCAN pin

dbcan is pinned to 5.1.2 with a version-pinned Zenodo copy of its database, because run_dbcan's official mirror only ever hosts the current one, and moving to 5.2.x is not a drop-in swap. See Annotation for what the two versions call differently.

docs.title: Fetching everything in one step
docs.text:
Each database is normally fetched by the first run that needs it. The download_all target fetches all of them at once, mobilome data sets included, and runs nothing else:

snakemake download_all --sdm conda --cores 4 --configfile config/config_custom.yaml

Name the target straight after snakemake: --sdm and --configfile each accept several values, so a target written after them would be read as one of those.

It asks for exactly what this config would download. The same switches decide, so nothing that a directories.*_db copy replaces, and nothing for a layer that is off, is fetched. Run it from the directory you will launch the real run from, with the same config (and the same --conda-prefix, if you use one), so the run finds the databases and the download environments already in place. A run whose jobs have no internet at all, for example a whole run inside one cluster batch job, also needs every other environment built beforehand, with --conda-create-envs-only: download_all builds only the environments of the download steps. Both steps are in Preparation, on a computer with internet.

Two things it does not fetch:

  • the five databases you download by hand, above;
  • the Medaka model weights in the long-read modes. The model check that downloads them reads the filtered long reads, so it cannot run before they exist. A long-read run with no internet needs that check to have run once on a computer with internet, or parameters.<mode>.medaka_model: false.

Every download rule is a local rule: when a cluster executor sends the other jobs to compute nodes, the downloads still run on the computer that runs Snakemake, so an ordinary cluster run needs internet only there.

docs.title: Pointing at a copy you already hold
docs.text:
Set any of these and the corresponding download is skipped entirely.

Key Point it at Worth setting because directories.checkv_db the parent directory holding the versioned folder, e.g. /db/checkv/ containing checkv-db-v1.5/ the official host is often down directories.vs2_db what virsorter setup produced (~10 GB) only read when phage.caller: virsorter2 directories.antismash_db what download-antismash-databases produced large directories.dbcan_db a dbCAN database matching the version in links.dbcan_link avoids a repeat download per project directories.card_db an extracted CARD database otherwise CARD is downloaded once into each output folder and kept there directories.genomad_db the inner genomad_db/ directory — the one holding version.txt and genomad_db.dbtype its downloader hard-codes one host with no mirror option, so a local copy is the only fallback

For these optional local paths, BacFlux checks during planning that the directory exists and contains database-specific files. The five required paths have more limited checks, as described under Practical notes.

Switching to another release in an existing output folder. A database the workflow downloaded, or linked from your copy, is kept in the output folder. Under --rerun-triggers mtime, a changed link or directories.*_db path does not replace it, and new samples are then analysed against the old copy. To switch, delete that database's folder in the output folder first, or start a new output folder. Deleting the folder re-runs nothing by itself: finished samples keep the results made with the old copy until the database is fetched again, by download_all or by the next run that needs it, such as one that adds a sample. From then on, every step that read it is redone; for CARD, read in illumina and hybrid, that is every sample in the folder from its PhiX screen onwards, the assembly included. The PhiX index is not downloaded but built, by the next run that screens a sample; download_all does not build it.

version.txt must be readable, not merely present

In a shared database directory it easily ends up mode 0640 while the big files beside it are world-readable. The check reads the file.

docs.title: The mobilome layers
docs.text: The optional mobilome module fetches up to five more data sets — the CONJscan models whenever the module runs, and ICEscan, TnCentral, ICEberg and ISOSDB only when you configure a source for each. Each has its own dir: key for a copy you already hold, and each writes a PROVENANCE.txt recording what actually arrived. See Optional layers.

docs.title: Practical notes
docs.text:
Downloads bring their own tools. The rules that fetch and unpack a database take wget, tar, gzip and bzip2 from workflow/envs/download.yaml, or from the tool's own environment for geNomad, VirSorter2 and CheckV; the mobilome layers fetch with curl and unzip from theirs. The computer needs nothing beyond the standard Unix utilities (Installation).

A wrong required path is not always caught at parse time. The five directories.*_db values are read but not opened while the plan is built. Some are then caught by the dry run because they are named as rule inputs — a blast_db with no nodes.dmp beside it fails there — and the rest surface when the tool runs. A dry run that reaches the job table means the plan is sound, not that every database is complete.

Disk. The five databases under The five you download take about 530 GB with the full Bakta database and about 450 GB with the light one, mostly core_nt and GTDB; actual usage depends on the nucleotide database release. The light Bakta database costs some annotation depth. The databases BacFlux fetches into output_dir add about 20 GB, before any analysis output.

  • Troubleshooting — what a missing or half-extracted database looks like when it fails.

docs.title: Coming from v1
docs.text:
This page explains migration from BacFlux 1.x, FastaFlux, BacFluxL or BacFluxL+. For a new installation, start with Installation.

Version 2.0.0 brings the four workflows into one repository, one mode each. The analysis steps, the thresholds and the decontamination policy came across as they were — given the same reads, tool versions, read mode and thread count, each read-based mode reproduced its predecessor's assembly byte for byte (Rationale). What changed is how a run is configured and where its output lands.

Terms used on this page

ONT Oxford Nanopore Technologies — the long-read sequencing platform DOI digital object identifier — the permanent handle a Zenodo record is cited by GTDB Genome Taxonomy Database, the reference used for taxonomic placement Was Now BacFlux — Illumina reads mode: illumina FastaFlux — pre-assembled contigs mode: contigs BacFluxL — ONT reads mode: nanopore BacFluxL+ — Illumina + ONT mode: hybrid

The BacFluxL and BacFluxL+ repositories are retired in favour of this one. Their Zenodo DOIs stay valid, so an analysis already published with either remains citable and reproducible — cite the record you actually ran.

docs.title: 1. Start your config again
docs.text:
A v1 config will not run v2. It has no mode: key, and v2 stops at parse time without one:

KeyError in file ".../workflow/rules/shared/00_common.smk", line …:
'mode'

Version 2 requires an explicit mode. An existing config/config_custom.yaml is ignored by Git and may therefore still contain the older configuration. Back it up before creating a new copy of the current template:

# If config_custom.yaml already exists, first save it under a separate name.
cp config/config.yaml config/config_custom.yaml

Then copy your database paths across by hand. The file is organised in sections — mode, input, directories, links, resources, parameters, phage, mobilome — and every key carries an inline comment saying which modes read it, so it is worth reading rather than pasting into. Every key is also listed in Configuration.

If you cloned fresh, none of this applies: there is no old file to collide with.

docs.title: 2. The mode lives in the config, not on the command line
docs.text:
One launch command runs all four modes:

snakemake --sdm conda --configfile config/config_custom.yaml --cores 24

Two things to know about it:

  • --cores alone is the CPU ceiling. Do not add --jobs/-j. For a local run --jobs is an alias for --cores, not an independent "N jobs of M cores each" setting, and passing both lets rules oversubscribe the machine. Every CPU-bound rule now declares Snakemake's built-in threads:, which is what --cores enforces. The measurement is on Running BacFlux.
  • --snakefile is never needed. workflow/Snakefile is found automatically from the repository root, and it dispatches on mode.

docs.title: 3. Relative paths resolve from where you launch
docs.text:
BacFlux no longer uses Snakemake's workdir: directive, so the process never changes directory. A relative input path now resolves against the directory you launched from, which is what most people expect. directories.output_dir may still be relative; it is resolved to an absolute path for you.

One consequence is easy to miss: the conda environments have moved. Snakemake creates them under .snakemake/conda in the launch directory. Launching from the same place each time is what stops the environments being rebuilt; --conda-prefix /some/path puts them somewhere specific, for example shared between projects.

docs.title: 4. The output directory is renumbered
docs.text:
All technology-specific work is now grouped under two fixed parents, so every shared stage has the same number in every mode. Previously each workflow had a different number of front-end stages, so the shared stages were numbered differently in each.

Was (short-read v1) Now 01.pre-processing 01.reads 02.assembly 02.assembly 03.post-processing 02.assembly/{sample}/eval and 02.assembly/{sample}/contaminants 04.taxonomy 03.taxonomy 05.annotation 04.annotation 06.AMR 05.amr 07.plasmids 06.plasmids 08.phages 07.phages — 08.mobilome (new, opt-in) 09.report 09.report

The delivered genome is now always 02.assembly/{sample}/contigs_final.fasta, whichever mode produced it, and the shared stages from 03 onwards analyse that genome.

There is no in-place upgrade. Point output_dir at a fresh directory rather than trying to reuse an old one. workflow/scripts/clean_workdir.sh recognises the four older layouts as well as the current one, so an old output directory can still be cleaned down to results and archived.

docs.title: 5. Everything else worth knowing before the first v2 run
docs.text:
Change What to do Sample names may contain underscores (and dots). Fifteen characters are still refused: * # @ % ^ / ! ? & : ; \| < > and space nothing, unless you had renamed files to avoid underscores GTDB R232 with GTDB-Tk 2.7.2 download R232; the pinned version rejects older releases Bakta database v6.0 with Bakta 1.12.1 download v6.0 The virus caller is selectable. VirSorter2 stays the default; geNomad is opt-in, and choosing it also produces a Platon + geNomad plasmid concordance table nothing, unless you want geNomad Phage calling now reads the delivered genome, contigs_final.fasta, in every mode. v1 BacFlux (Illumina) scanned the draft before contaminant contigs were removed nothing; phage calls on contigs that decontamination removes no longer appear Six databases can be supplied from a copy you already hold — checkv_db, vs2_db, antismash_db, dbcan_db, card_db, genomad_db set the ones you have; the download is then skipped The mobilome module is new and off by default see the mobilome module QUAST now runs in nanopore mode, which never had it, and in hybrid it evaluates the delivered genome as well as the Illumina draft nothing

One downstream difference is deliberate and appears in the two long-read modes: Bakta gains or loses a single feature, because it is now handed a --replicons table declaring a closed chromosome circular. That makes its gene caller run in closed mode, which shifts a couple of marginal start codons. It is one feature in several thousand in the comparison on Rationale. Changes in gene boundaries should be considered when comparing annotations across versions.

docs.text:
